t.4.1: The Blessed Lord said: I declared this imperishable yoga to Vivasvān; Vivasvān told it to Manu, and Manu spoke it to Ikṣvāku.
t.4.2: Thus received through succession, this the royal sages knew. But that yoga, through a great lapse of time, has been lost here in this world, O scorcher of foes.
t.4.3: That very same ancient yoga has today been declared by me to you, since you are my devotee and my friend; for this is the supreme secret.
t.4.4: Arjuna said: Your birth was later, and the birth of Vivasvān was earlier. How am I to understand this, that you declared it in the beginning?
t.4.5: The Blessed Lord said: Many births of mine have passed away, and of yours too, Arjuna. I know them all, but you do not know them, O scorcher of foes.
t.4.6: Though I am unborn and my self is imperishable, though I am the Lord of all beings, yet, presiding over my own nature, I come into being through my own māyā.
t.4.7: Whenever there is a decline of dharma, O Bhārata, and a rise of adharma, then I send forth myself.
t.4.8: For the protection of the good and for the destruction of evildoers, for the sake of firmly establishing dharma, I come into being age after age.
t.4.9: He who thus knows in truth my divine birth and action, O Arjuna, does not go to rebirth on leaving the body; he comes to me.
t.4.10: Freed from passion, fear and anger, absorbed in me and taking refuge in me, many, purified by the austerity of knowledge, have attained my state of being.
t.4.11: In whatever way people approach me, in that very way I share myself with them. Everywhere, O Pārtha, people follow my path.
t.4.13: The fourfold order of society was created by me according to the division of qualities and actions. Though I am its maker, know me to be the non-doer, the imperishable.
t.4.12: Those longing for the success of their actions, worshipping the deities here, find that in the human world success born of action comes quickly indeed.
t.4.14: Actions do not stain me, nor do I have any longing for the fruit of action. One who knows me thus is not bound by actions.
t.4.15: Knowing this, even the ancient seekers of liberation performed action. Therefore you too must perform action, just as it was performed of old by the ancients.
t.4.16: What is action and what is inaction? Even the wise are bewildered about this. I shall explain to you that action, knowing which you will be freed from what is inauspicious.
t.4.17: One must indeed understand what action is, and one must understand what wrong action is, and one must understand what inaction is; deep and hard to fathom is the way of action.
t.4.18: One who sees inaction in action and action in inaction is wise among men; he is disciplined in yoga and a performer of all actions.
t.4.19: He whose every undertaking is free from desire and its motivating intent, whose actions have been burned up in the fire of knowledge, him the wise call a learned man.
t.4.20: Having abandoned attachment to the fruits of action, ever content and dependent on nothing, he does nothing at all, even though fully engaged in action.
t.4.21: Free from desire, with mind and self controlled, having abandoned all possessions, performing action with the body alone, he incurs no sin.
t.4.22: Content with whatever comes to him by chance, having passed beyond the pairs of opposites, free from envy, and even-minded in success and failure, he is not bound, even though he acts.
t.4.23: For one whose attachment is gone, who is liberated, whose mind is established in knowledge, and who performs action for the sake of sacrifice, the whole of his karma dissolves away completely.
t.4.24: The offering is Brahman, the oblation is Brahman, poured by Brahman into the fire that is Brahman; Brahman alone is to be reached by him who is wholly absorbed in action that is Brahman.
t.4.25: Some yogins worship through sacrifice offered to the gods alone; others offer sacrifice itself, by means of sacrifice, into the fire of Brahman.
t.4.26: Some offer the senses, hearing and the rest, into the fires of restraint; others offer the objects of sense, sound and the rest, into the fires of the senses.
t.4.27: Others offer all the actions of the senses and the actions of the vital breath into the fire of the yoga of self-restraint, kindled by knowledge.
t.4.29: Others offer the prāṇa into the apāna, and likewise the apāna into the prāṇa; having restrained the courses of prāṇa and apāna, they are wholly devoted to prāṇāyāma.
t.4.28: Some offer their material possessions as sacrifice, others their austerity, and still others the practice of yoga; while ascetics of strict vows offer scriptural study and knowledge as their sacrifice.
t.4.30: Others, restraining their food, offer their life-breaths into the life-breaths. All of these are knowers of sacrifice, their impurities destroyed by sacrifice.
t.4.31: Those who eat the nectar that remains from sacrifice go to the eternal Brahman. This world is not for one who does not sacrifice; how then the other, O best of the Kurus?
t.4.32: Thus many kinds of sacrifices are spread out at the mouth of Brahman. Know them all to be born of action; knowing thus, you will be liberated.
t.4.33: Better than the sacrifice made of material things is the sacrifice of knowledge, O Paraṃtapa; all action without exception, O Pārtha, culminates in knowledge.
t.4.34: Know that by prostration, by thorough inquiry, and by service; the wise, the seers of truth, will instruct you in knowledge.
t.4.35: Knowing that, O Pāṇḍava, you will not again fall into delusion like this; and by that you will see all beings without exception in the Self, and then in me.
t.4.36: Even if you were the very worst of sinners, more sinful than all evildoers, you would cross over all wickedness by the raft of knowledge alone.
t.4.37: Just as a blazing fire reduces firewood to ashes, O Arjuna, so does the fire of knowledge reduce all actions to ashes.
t.4.38: Truly, nothing in this world is found that is as purifying as knowledge. One who is perfected in yoga finds that knowledge within himself, of his own accord, in the course of time.
t.4.39: The one who has faith, devoted to it and with senses restrained, attains knowledge; having attained knowledge, he quickly reaches supreme peace.
t.4.40: The ignorant one, the one without faith, and the one whose self is full of doubt perish. For the doubting soul there is neither this world nor the next, nor any happiness.
t.4.41: Actions do not bind one who has renounced actions through yoga, whose doubts have been cut asunder by knowledge, and who is self-possessed, O Dhanaṃjaya.
t.4.42: Therefore, having cut asunder with the sword of knowledge this doubt of the self, born of ignorance and lodged in the heart, take refuge in yoga and arise, O Bhārata!
